newsitem.title: KENYA: Small investors to gain on Serena Kenya flotation.
newsitem.headline: Small investors to gain on Serena Kenya flotation.

text.p: Small investors awarded shares this week in the initial public offering of the Aga Khan-owned Serena Lodges & Hotels can make a swift profit if institutional interest remains, brokers said on Thursday.
Small investors gained most when offers for the four-times oversubscribed flotation ended on Monday, with nearly 8,000 individuals being awarded the minimum 500-share lot.
Over 8,000 bigger investors -- including 738 institutionals -- were disappointed to receive just 640 shares each from their applications.
Their disappointment highlights a rift between government and the private sector on the issue of who should control the bulk of Kenyan stock market capital.
Kenya's rulers have made no secret of their desire to see more small investors -- particularly local people -- have a stake in the economy, especially with a series of privatisation schemes ahead.
But institutional investors are seeking bigger block-buys in order to protect their stake from the volatility of frequent trading on small profits.
"Given an oversubscription of four times, at least we expected a more equitable spread," one broker said.
A major bone of contention among foreign investors is the heavy costs incurred by tying up funds for weeks during the offer, leaving them exposed to exchange rate fluctuations.

"A good example of an issue where foreign investors felt they were treated very badly is the Kenya Commercial Bank in October when they got only 10 percent of what they applied for after three weeks," said John Munge, managing director of brokers Shah Munge & Partners.
"A practical way for the future would be for an issue to close as soon as it is oversubscribed or for brokers to take the responsibility to honour client commitments upon allotment."

In Serena's case, brokers say renewed institutional interest now depends on whether investors believe the group can realise an optimistic earnings forecast in an industry that is facing stiff competition from tourist destinations south of Kenya.

Government-owned Kenya Tourism Development Corporation sold 9,025,100 shares -- a 23.3 percent stake -- in Tourism Promotion Services (TPS), which owns the Serena group, at a discounted price of 13 shillings per share.
TPS is 83 percent owned by the Aga Khan and has a 76.7 percent stake in Serena.

The Serena group has projected an increased turnover of 1.27 billion shillings ($23.96 million) and an after tax profit of 66.3 million shillings for the year ending 31 December 1997 -- up from last year's turnover of 1.16 billion shillings and after tax profit of 41.2 million shillings.
Market analysts pointed out the distribution had widened Serena's spectrum of shareholders and given it a retail profile much fancied by speculators.
"Speculators could make quick bucks if we get big buying orders from foreign and institutional investors," a broker said.
Serena Lodges & Hotels operates two luxury hotels in the capital Nairobi, a resort in Mombasa and three lodges in the game reserves of Masai Mara, Amboseli and Samburu.
The Serena flotation follows the successful flotation of Kenya Airways, Kenya Commercial Bank and National Bank of Kenya.
Other issues scheduled for the year include Kenya Reinsurance Corporation, Chemilil Sugar Company and Mumias Sugar Company.
